question_en: Let \(a_n=\frac13+\frac17+\cdots+\frac{1}{4n-1}\), for \(n=1,2,\ldots\). Which of the following is true?
question_gu: Let \(a_n=\frac13+\frac17+\cdots+\frac{1}{4n-1}\), for \(n=1,2,\ldots\). Which of the following is true?
options_en: \(\{a_n\}\) is unbounded having one limit point zero
\(\{a_n\}\) is bounded having one limit point zero
\(\{a_n\}\) is a Cauchy sequence of rationals converging to an irrational number
options_gu: \(\{a_n\}\) is unbounded having one limit point zero
\(\{a_n\}\) is bounded having one limit point zero
\(\{a_n\}\) is a Cauchy sequence of rationals converging to an irrational number
explanation_en: The terms are positive and the partial sums increase. Since \(\sum_{k=1}^{n}\frac{1}{4k-1}\) diverges (its terms are comparable to \(1/(4k)\)), the sequence of partial sums is unbounded and cannot be Cauchy. Thus (D) is true.
explanation_gu: આંશિક સરવાળા વધતા જાય છે. કારણ કે \(\sum_{k=1}^{n}\frac{1}{4k-1}\) harmonic series સાથે સરખાવી શકાય છે અને diverge થાય છે, તેથી \(\{a_n\}\) unbounded છે અને Cauchy sequence નથી. એટલે (D) સાચો વિકલ્પ છે.

tip_en: A convergent sequence must be Cauchy and bounded; divergence of the partial sums rules both out.
tip_gu: દરેક convergent sequence Cauchy અને bounded હોય છે; આ partial sums diverge થાય છે.

question_en: Every rational number \(x\) can be written in lowest terms as \(x=m/n\), where \(n>0\) and \(m,n\) are integers without a common divisor. Define \(f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) by \(f(x)=0\) if \(x\) is irrational and \(f(m/n)=1/n\) if \(x=m/n\) is rational in lowest terms (take \(n=1\) when \(x=0\)). Then \(f\) is:
question_gu: Every rational number \(x\) can be written in lowest terms as \(x=m/n\), where \(n>0\) and \(m,n\) are integers without a common divisor. Define \(f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) by \(f(x)=0\) if \(x\) is irrational and \(f(m/n)=1/n\) if \(x=m/n\) is rational in lowest terms (take \(n=1\) when \(x=0\)). Then \(f\) is:
options_en: Continuous only at every irrational point
Continuous only at every rational point
Discontinuous at every point of \(\mathbb R\)
options_gu: Continuous only at every irrational point
Continuous only at every rational point
Discontinuous at every point of \(\mathbb R\)
explanation_en: This is Thomae's function. At an irrational point, nearby rationals with large denominators have values \(1/n\) close to zero, while irrational points have value zero, so the function is continuous at every irrational. At a rational point, the function value is positive but arbitrarily close irrational points have value zero, so it is discontinuous at each rational.
explanation_gu: આ Thomae function છે. Irrational બિંદુ પાસે નજીકના rational numbersના reduced denominatorને મોટો બનાવી શકાય છે, તેથી \(1/n\to0\); irrational પર function value પણ 0 છે. તેથી દરેક irrational બિંદુએ continuity છે. Rational બિંદુએ function value positive છે, પરંતુ નજીકના irrational બિંદુઓ પર value 0 હોવાથી ત્યાં discontinuity છે.

tip_en: Thomae's function is continuous at irrational numbers and discontinuous at rational numbers.
tip_gu: Thomae function irrational બિંદુઓએ continuous અને rational બિંદુઓએ discontinuous છે.

question_en: The equation \(2x-1-\sin x=0\) has:
question_gu: The equation \(2x-1-\sin x=0\) has:
explanation_en: Let \(g(x)=2x-1-\sin x\). Then \(g'(x)=2-\cos x\ge1>0\), so g is strictly increasing and has at most one real root. Also, g(x) tends to −∞ as x tends to −∞ and +∞ as x tends to +∞, so by continuity it has a root. Hence exactly one real root.
explanation_gu: \(g(x)=2x-1-\sin x\) લો. ત્યારે \(g'(x)=2-\cos x\ge1>0\), એટલે g strictly increasing છે અને વધુમાં વધુ એક root હોઈ શકે. ઉપરાંત x→−∞ પર g→−∞ અને x→+∞ પર g→+∞; continuityથી root અસ્તિત્વમાં છે. તેથી ચોક્કસ એક real root છે.
review_note: Answer checked against the repository's official GSET final answer-key transcription; question wording/options remain unverified against the original question paper.
tip_en: Use the derivative to prove strict monotonicity, then use end behavior to establish existence.
tip_gu: Derivativeથી strict monotonicity સાબિત કરો અને end behaviorથી rootનું અસ્તિત્વ બતાવો.
source: GSET official September 2013 Mathematical Sciences Paper-II question paper and corrected final answer key

question_en: Suppose \(f_n(x)=\frac{x}{1+nx^2}\) and \(f(x)=0\) for all \(x\in\mathbb R\). Which statement about \(\{f_n\}\) is true?
question_gu: Suppose \(f_n(x)=\frac{x}{1+nx^2}\) and \(f(x)=0\) for all \(x\in\mathbb R\). Which statement about \(\{f_n\}\) is true?
options_en: \(f_n\) converges uniformly to f over \([-1,1]\) only
\(f_n\) converges pointwise but not uniformly over any interval containing zero
\(f_n\) converges uniformly to f only on some bounded interval \([-\lambda,\lambda]\), \(\lambda>0\)
\(f_n\) converges uniformly to f over all of \(\mathbb R\)
options_gu: \(f_n\) converges uniformly to f over \([-1,1]\) only
\(f_n\) converges pointwise but not uniformly over any interval containing zero
\(f_n\) converges uniformly to f only on some bounded interval \([-\lambda,\lambda]\), \(\lambda>0\)
\(f_n\) converges uniformly to f over all of \(\mathbb R\)
explanation_en: For all real x, \(|f_n(x)|=\frac{|x|}{1+nx^2}\). Its maximum occurs at \(|x|=1/\sqrt n\), giving \(\sup_{x\in\mathbb R}|f_n(x)|=1/(2\sqrt n)\to0\). Therefore the convergence to zero is uniform on the whole real line.
explanation_gu: દરેક real x માટે \(|f_n(x)|=\frac{|x|}{1+nx^2}\). Maximum \(|x|=1/\sqrt n\) પર મળે છે અને \(\sup_{x\in\mathbb R}|f_n(x)|=1/(2\sqrt n)\to0\). તેથી આખા real line પર uniform convergence થાય છે.
review_note: Answer checked against the repository's official GSET final answer-key transcription; question wording/options remain unverified against the original question paper.
tip_en: Uniform convergence can be proved by showing the supremum of the absolute error tends to zero.
tip_gu: Absolute errorનું supremum શૂન્ય તરફ જાય છે તે બતાવી uniform convergence સાબિત કરી શકાય.
source: GSET official September 2013 Mathematical Sciences Paper-II question paper and corrected final answer key

question_en: The equation \(|z-1|+|z+1|=2\sqrt2\) represents a:
question_gu: The equation \(|z-1|+|z+1|=2\sqrt2\) represents a:
explanation_en: In the complex plane, \(|z-1|\) and \(|z+1|\) are distances from the fixed points 1 and −1. The locus for which the sum of distances from two fixed foci is constant is an ellipse. Hence (C).
explanation_gu: Complex planeમાં \(|z-1|\) અને \(|z+1|\) અનુક્રમે 1 અને −1થી અંતર છે. બે fixed fociથી અંતરોનો સરવાળો constant હોય તે locus ellipse છે. તેથી (C).
review_note: Answer checked against the repository's official GSET final answer-key transcription; question wording/options remain unverified against the original question paper.
tip_en: Recognize conics by their distance definitions: an ellipse has a constant sum of distances to two foci.
tip_gu: Conic ઓળખો: ellipse માટે બે fociથી અંતરોનો સરવાળો constant હોય છે.
source: GSET official September 2013 Mathematical Sciences Paper-II question paper and corrected final answer key

question_en: Which of the following is true if the functions involved are complex-valued functions over the complex domain \(\mathbb C\)?
question_gu: નીચેના પૈકી કયું વિધાન સાચું છે, જો functions complex-valued હોય અને domain \(\mathbb C\) હોય?
explanation_en: For option (B), \(\sin z/z\) has a removable singularity at \(z=0\), since \(\lim_{z\to0}\sin z/z=1\). After defining its value at zero to be \(1\), it is entire, so its integral around the closed unit circle is \(0\) by Cauchy's theorem. Option (A) is false because \(|\cos z|\) is not bounded by \(1\) on the complex plane. In (C), the integrand has residue \(1\) at zero, so the integral is \(2\pi i\), not \(0\). Thus (B) is correct.
explanation_gu: વિકલ્પ (B)માં \(\sin z/z\) માટે \(z=0\) પર removable singularity છે, કારણ કે \(\lim_{z\to0}\sin z/z=1\). \(z=0\) પર તેનું મૂલ્ય \(1\) વ્યાખ્યાયિત કરતાં તે entire function બને છે. તેથી Cauchy's theorem મુજબ closed unit circle પર તેનું contour integral \(0\) છે. વિકલ્પ (A) ખોટો છે, કારણ કે complex plane પર \(|\cos z|\le1\) હંમેશા સાચું નથી. વિકલ્પ (C)માં residue \(1\) હોવાથી integral \(2\pi i\) થાય છે, \(0\) નહીં. તેથી (B) સાચો છે.
review_note: Question wording and all four options checked against official GSET September 2013 Paper-II PDF, printed page 7 (PDF page 7). Answer B matches the official corrected answer key. Answer checked against the repository's official GSET final answer-key transcription; question wording/options remain unverified against the original question paper.
tip_en: Use Cauchy's theorem only after checking analyticity inside and on the contour.
tip_gu: Contour integral માટે Cauchy's theorem વાપરતાં function contourની અંદર analytic છે કે નહીં તે તપાસો.
source: Official GSET Mathematical Sciences Paper-II, September 2013

question_en: If \(f(z)=\frac{2z}{(z+4)(z-1)^2}\), then the residue of f(z) at \(z=1\) is:
question_gu: If \(f(z)=\frac{2z}{(z+4)(z-1)^2}\), then the residue of f(z) at \(z=1\) is:
explanation_en: At z = 1 there is a double pole. Write \(f(z)=h(z)/(z-1)^2\), where \(h(z)=2z/(z+4)\). The residue is \(h'(1)\). Since \(h'(z)=8/(z+4)^2\), the residue is \(8/25\), option (B).
review_note: Answer checked against the repository's official GSET final answer-key transcription; question wording/options remain unverified against the original question paper.
tip_en: For a double pole of the form h(z)/(z−a)², the residue is h′(a).
tip_gu: \(h(z)/(z-a)^2\) સ્વરૂપના double pole માટે residue \(h'(a)\) હોય છે.
source: GSET official September 2013 Mathematical Sciences Paper-II question paper and corrected final answer key

question_en: The number of \(3\times3\) matrices with eigenvalues \(1,\sqrt2,\sqrt3\) is:
question_gu: The number of \(3\times3\) matrices with eigenvalues \(1,\sqrt2,\sqrt3\) is:
explanation_en: The eigenvalues are distinct, so a diagonal matrix with these entries exists. Conjugating it by invertible matrices produces matrices with the same eigenvalues; there are infinitely many such matrices. Therefore (D).
explanation_gu: આ ત્રણ eigenvalues distinct છે, તેથી diagonal matrix \(D=\operatorname{diag}(1,\sqrt2,\sqrt3)\) શક્ય છે. Invertible matricesથી similarity transformation કરવાથી એ જ eigenvalues ધરાવતી infinitely many matrices મળે છે. તેથી (D).
review_note: Answer checked against the repository's official GSET final answer-key transcription; question wording/options remain unverified against the original question paper.
tip_en: Similarity transformations preserve eigenvalues; distinct invertible changes of basis can generate infinitely many matrices.
tip_gu: Similarity transformation eigenvalues જાળવે છે; જુદા invertible change-of-basisથી અનંત matrices મળી શકે.
source: GSET official September 2013 Mathematical Sciences Paper-II question paper and corrected final answer key

question_en: For what value of \(\lambda\) does the set of vectors \(\{(1,2,3,\lambda),(3,2,1,\lambda),(2,6,10,3),(1,1,1,1)\}\) become linearly dependent?
question_gu: For what value of \(\lambda\) does the set of vectors \(\{(1,2,3,\lambda),(3,2,1,\lambda),(2,6,10,3),(1,1,1,1)\}\) become linearly dependent?
explanation_en: Place the four vectors as rows of a 4×4 matrix. Its second and third coordinate columns satisfy C₃=2C₂−C₁: for each row, the third coordinate is twice the second minus the first. Thus the columns are linearly dependent, the determinant is zero for every λ, and the four vectors are linearly dependent for any value of λ.
explanation_gu: ચાર vectorsને 4×4 matrixની rows તરીકે મૂકો. તેમાં બીજા અને ત્રીજા coordinate columns માટે (C_3=2C_2-C_1) છે: દરેક vectorમાં ત્રીજો coordinate, બીજા coordinateના બમણામાંથી પહેલો coordinate ઘટાડવાથી મળે છે. તેથી columns linearly dependent છે, determinant દરેક (lambda) માટે zero છે અને vectors કોઈપણ (lambda) માટે linearly dependent છે.
review_note: Answer checked against the repository's official GSET final answer-key transcription; question wording/options remain unverified against the original question paper.
tip_en: Look for a fixed linear relation among matrix columns before expanding a determinant.
tip_gu: Determinant expand કરતાં પહેલાં matrixના columns વચ્ચે fixed linear relation છે કે નહીં તે જુઓ.
source: GSET official September 2013 Mathematical Sciences Paper-II question paper and corrected final answer key

question_en: The real values of \(k\) for which the linear system \((k+1)x-y+2z=0\), \(-2x+y+z=0\), \(k^2x+3z=0\) has a non-trivial solution are:
question_gu: The real values of \(k\) for which the linear system \((k+1)x-y+2z=0\), \(-2x+y+z=0\), \(k^2x+3z=0\) has a non-trivial solution are:
explanation_en: A non-trivial solution requires the coefficient determinant to vanish. For \(A=\begin{bmatrix}k+1&-1&2\\-2&1&1\\k^2&0&3\end{bmatrix}\), \(\det A=-3(k^2-k+1)\). But \(k^2-k+1=(k-1/2)^2+3/4>0\) for every real k, so the determinant never vanishes. There is no real k with a non-trivial solution; option (A).
explanation_gu: Non-trivial solution માટે coefficient determinant શૂન્ય હોવો જોઈએ. \(A=\begin{bmatrix}k+1&-1&2\\-2&1&1\\k^2&0&3\end{bmatrix}\) માટે \(\det A=-3(k^2-k+1)\). પરંતુ \(k^2-k+1=(k-1/2)^2+3/4>0\) દરેક real k માટે, તેથી determinant ક્યારેય શૂન્ય નથી. એટલે કોઈ real k માટે non-trivial solution નથી; વિકલ્પ (A).
review_note: Answer checked against the repository's official GSET final answer-key transcription; question wording/options remain unverified against the original question paper.
tip_en: A homogeneous linear system has a non-trivial solution only if its coefficient determinant is zero.
tip_gu: Homogeneous linear systemમાં non-trivial solution માટે coefficient determinant શૂન્ય હોવો જરૂરી છે.
source: GSET official September 2013 Mathematical Sciences Paper-II question paper and corrected final answer key

question_en: The real quadratic form \(3x_1^2+3x_2^2+6x_3^2-2x_1x_2-4x_1x_3\) is:
question_gu: The real quadratic form \(3x_1^2+3x_2^2+6x_3^2-2x_1x_2-4x_1x_3\) is:
explanation_en: The associated symmetric matrix is \(A=\begin{bmatrix}3&-1&-2\\-1&3&0\\-2&0&6\end{bmatrix}\). Its leading principal minors are \(3>0\), \(\det\begin{bmatrix}3&-1\\-1&3\end{bmatrix}=8>0\), and \(\det A=36>0\). By Sylvester's criterion, the quadratic form is positive definite.
explanation_gu: Associated symmetric matrix \(A=\begin{bmatrix}3&-1&-2\\-1&3&0\\-2&0&6\end{bmatrix}\) છે. Leading principal minors \(3>0\), \(\det\begin{bmatrix}3&-1\\-1&3\end{bmatrix}=8>0\), અને \(\det A=36>0\) છે. Sylvester criterion પ્રમાણે quadratic form positive definite છે.
review_note: Answer checked against the repository's official GSET final answer-key transcription; question wording/options remain unverified against the original question paper.
tip_en: For a real symmetric matrix, positivity of all leading principal minors proves positive definiteness.
tip_gu: Real symmetric matrix માટે બધા leading principal minors positive હોય તો quadratic form positive definite છે.
source: GSET official September 2013 Mathematical Sciences Paper-II question paper and corrected final answer key

question_en: If \(A=\begin{bmatrix}-3&-7&-5\\2&4&3\\1&2&2\end{bmatrix}\), then which of the following is true?
question_gu: જો \(A=\begin{bmatrix}-3&-7&-5\\2&4&3\\1&2&2\end{bmatrix}\) હોય, તો નીચેના પૈકી કયું વિધાન સાચું છે?
options_en: \(\begin{bmatrix}-3\\1\\1\end{bmatrix}\) is an eigenvector for an eigenvalue of multiplicity \(1\)
\(\begin{bmatrix}-3\\1\\1\end{bmatrix}\) is an eigenvector for an eigenvalue of multiplicity \(2\)
\(\begin{bmatrix}-3\\1\\1\end{bmatrix}\) is an eigenvector for an eigenvalue of multiplicity \(3\)
\(\begin{bmatrix}-3\\1\\1\end{bmatrix}\) is not an eigenvector for any eigenvalue
options_gu: \(\begin{bmatrix}-3\\1\\1\end{bmatrix}\) is an eigenvector for an eigenvalue of multiplicity \(1\)
\(\begin{bmatrix}-3\\1\\1\end{bmatrix}\) is an eigenvector for an eigenvalue of multiplicity \(2\)
\(\begin{bmatrix}-3\\1\\1\end{bmatrix}\) is an eigenvector for an eigenvalue of multiplicity \(3\)
\(\begin{bmatrix}-3\\1\\1\end{bmatrix}\) is not an eigenvector for any eigenvalue
explanation_en: Let \(v=(-3,1,1)^T\). Direct multiplication gives \(Av=v\), so \(v\) is an eigenvector with eigenvalue \(\lambda=1\). The characteristic polynomial is \(\det(\lambda I-A)=(\lambda-1)^3\). Hence the eigenvalue \(1\) has algebraic multiplicity \(3\), and option (C) is correct.
explanation_gu: \(v=(-3,1,1)^T\) લો. સીધી matrix multiplicationથી \(Av=v\) મળે છે, એટલે \(v\), eigenvalue \(\lambda=1\) માટે eigenvector છે. Characteristic polynomial \(\det(\lambda I-A)=(\lambda-1)^3\) છે. તેથી eigenvalue \(1\)ની algebraic multiplicity \(3\) છે અને વિકલ્પ (C) સાચો છે.
review_note: Matrix, vector, and all four options checked against official GSET September 2013 Paper-II PDF, printed page 9 (PDF page 9). Answer C matches the official corrected key. Answer checked against the repository's official GSET final answer-key transcription; question wording/options remain unverified against the original question paper.
tip_en: Verify eigenvectors by Av = λv and multiplicity using the characteristic polynomial.
tip_gu: Eigenvector માટે Av = λv અને multiplicity માટે characteristic polynomial તપાસો.
source: Official GSET Mathematical Sciences Paper-II, September 2013

question_en: The probability distribution of a random variable \(X\) is \(P(X=0)=\alpha\) and \(P(X=2)=1-\alpha\). If the variance of \(X\) is 1, then \(\alpha\) is:
question_gu: The probability distribution of a random variable \(X\) is \(P(X=0)=\alpha\) and \(P(X=2)=1-\alpha\). If the variance of \(X\) is 1, then \(\alpha\) is:
explanation_en: Here E(X) = 2(1−α) and E(X²) = 4(1−α). Thus Var(X) = E(X²) − [E(X)]² = 4(1−α) − 4(1−α)² = 4α(1−α). Set this equal to 1: 4α(1−α)=1, so (2α−1)²=0 and α=1/2.
explanation_gu: અહીં (E(X)=2(1-\alpha)) અને (E(X^2)=4(1-\alpha)). તેથી (Var(X)=E(X^2)-[E(X)]^2=4(1-\alpha)-4(1-\alpha)^2=4\alpha(1-\alpha)). Variance 1 હોવાથી (4\alpha(1-\alpha)=1), એટલે ((2\alpha-1)^2=0) અને (alpha=1/2).
review_note: Answer checked against the repository's official GSET final answer-key transcription; question wording/options remain unverified against the original question paper.
tip_en: For a two-point distribution, calculate E(X) and E(X²), then use Var(X)=E(X²)−[E(X)]².
tip_gu: Two-point distribution માટે પહેલાં E(X) અને E(X²) કાઢો, પછી Var(X)=E(X²)−[E(X)]² વાપરો.
source: GSET official September 2013 Mathematical Sciences Paper-II question paper and corrected final answer key

question_en: Suppose \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\) is a random sample from the uniform distribution \(U(0,\theta)\). What is the sampling distribution function of \(Y=\max(X_1,\ldots,X_n)\)?
question_gu: Suppose \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\) is a random sample from the uniform distribution \(U(0,\theta)\). What is the sampling distribution function of \(Y=\max(X_1,\ldots,X_n)\)?
explanation_en: For 0<y<θ, the maximum is at most y exactly when every sample value is at most y. By independence, P(Y≤y) = ∏ᵢP(Xᵢ≤y) = (y/θ)ⁿ. Therefore G(y;θ)=(y/θ)ⁿ on this interval.
explanation_gu: (0<y<\theta) માટે (Y\le y) ત્યારે જ થાય જ્યારે દરેક sample value (y) કરતાં નાનું કે સમાન હોય. Independenceથી (P(Y\le y)=\prod_i P(X_i\le y)=(y/\theta)^n). તેથી (G(y;\theta)=(y/\theta)^n).
review_note: Answer checked against the repository's official GSET final answer-key transcription; question wording/options remain unverified against the original question paper.
tip_en: The CDF of the maximum of independent variables is the product of their individual CDFs.
tip_gu: Independent variablesના maximumનું CDF તેમના individual CDFના product બરાબર હોય છે.
source: GSET official September 2013 Mathematical Sciences Paper-II question paper and corrected final answer key

question_en: Two fair dice are thrown simultaneously. Let \(X_i\) denote the score on the i-th die, \(i=1,2\), and let \(X=\max(X_1,X_2)\). Find \(P(X_1=2, X=2)\).
question_gu: Two fair dice are thrown simultaneously. Let \(X_i\) denote the score on the i-th die, \(i=1,2\), and let \(X=\max(X_1,X_2)\). Find \(P(X_1=2, X=2)\).
explanation_en: The event X₁=2 and X=2 requires the first die to show 2 and the second die to show either 1 or 2. There are 2 favourable outcomes among 36 equally likely ordered outcomes, so the probability is 2/36=1/18.
explanation_gu: (X_1=2) અને (X=2) માટે પ્રથમ dice પર 2 અને બીજા dice પર 1 અથવા 2 આવવું જોઈએ. કુલ 36 equally likely ordered outcomesમાંથી 2 અનુકૂળ outcomes છે. તેથી probability (2/36=1/18).
review_note: Answer checked against the repository's official GSET final answer-key transcription; question wording/options remain unverified against the original question paper.
tip_en: Translate a maximum condition into restrictions on every individual die.
tip_gu: Maximumની conditionને દરેક dice પર લાગુ પડતી શરતોમાં ફેરવો.
source: GSET official September 2013 Mathematical Sciences Paper-II question paper and corrected final answer key

question_en: If \(X\) and \(Y\) are independent random variables with distribution functions \(F\) and \(G\), respectively, then the distribution function of \(X+Y\) is:
question_gu: If \(X\) and \(Y\) are independent random variables with distribution functions \(F\) and \(G\), respectively, then the distribution function of \(X+Y\) is:
explanation_en: The CDF of the sum is P(X+Y≤x). Conditioning on Y=y gives P(X≤x−y)=F(x−y). Integrating with respect to the distribution of Y yields F_{X+Y}(x)=∫F(x−y)dG(y), option (B).
explanation_gu: Sumનું CDF (P(X+Y\le x)) છે. (Y=y) પર condition કરીએ તો (P(X\le x-y)=F(x-y)). Yના distribution પ્રમાણે integrate કરતાં (F_{X+Y}(x)=\int F(x-y)\,dG(y)) મળે છે; વિકલ્પ (B).
review_note: Answer checked against the repository's official GSET final answer-key transcription; question wording/options remain unverified against the original question paper.
tip_en: For a sum, condition on one variable and shift the argument of the other CDF.
tip_gu: Sum માટે એક variable પર condition કરો અને બીજા CDFના argumentમાં (x-y) મૂકો.
source: GSET official September 2013 Mathematical Sciences Paper-II question paper and corrected final answer key

question_en: Let \(X\) be Poisson with \(E(X)=\lambda\), and let \(Y\) be a geometric random variable with \(P(Y=0)=P(X=0)\). Which relation is true?
question_gu: Let \(X\) be Poisson with \(E(X)=\lambda\), and let \(Y\) be a geometric random variable with \(P(Y=0)=P(X=0)\). Which relation is true?
explanation_en: For a Poisson variable, P(X=0)=e⁻λ. A geometric variable supported on 0,1,2,… with P(Y=0)=p has E(Y)=(1−p)/p and Var(Y)=(1−p)/p², so Var(Y)=E(Y)/p. Setting p=e⁻λ gives Var(Y)=e^λ E(Y), option (C).
explanation_gu: Poisson variable માટે (P(X=0)=e^{-\lambda}). (P(Y=0)=p) ધરાવતા (0,1,2,\ldots) પરના geometric variable માટે (E(Y)=(1-p)/p) અને (Var(Y)=(1-p)/p^2=E(Y)/p). (p=e^{-\lambda}) મૂક્તાં (Var(Y)=e^\lambda E(Y)), એટલે (C).
review_note: Answer checked against the repository's official GSET final answer-key transcription; question wording/options remain unverified against the original question paper.
tip_en: Check which geometric-distribution convention is being used; here Y starts at zero.
tip_gu: Geometric distribution કઈ conventionથી વ્યાખ્યાયિત છે તે તપાસો; અહીં Yની શરૂઆત zeroથી થાય છે.
source: GSET official September 2013 Mathematical Sciences Paper-II question paper and corrected final answer key

question_en: Let A and B be independent events with \(P(A\cap B)=\frac16\). If \(P(A\cap B^c)=\frac13\), which statement is true?
question_gu: Let A and B be independent events with \(P(A\cap B)=\frac16\). If \(P(A\cap B^c)=\frac13\), which statement is true?
explanation_en: Since P(A)=P(A∩B)+P(A∩Bᶜ)=1/6+1/3=1/2. Independence gives P(A∩B)=P(A)P(B), so 1/6=(1/2)P(B), hence P(B)=1/3. Option (A).
explanation_gu: (P(A)=P(A\cap B)+P(A\cap B^c)=1/6+1/3=1/2). Independenceથી (P(A\cap B)=P(A)P(B)), એટલે (1/6=(1/2)P(B)), તેથી (P(B)=1/3). વિકલ્પ (A).
review_note: Answer checked against the repository's official GSET final answer-key transcription; question wording/options remain unverified against the original question paper.
tip_en: First reconstruct P(A) by splitting A into A∩B and A∩Bᶜ, then apply independence.
tip_gu: પહેલાં (A)ને (A\cap B) અને (A\cap B^c)માં વહેંચીને P(A) કાઢો; પછી independence વાપરો.
source: GSET official September 2013 Mathematical Sciences Paper-II question paper and corrected final answer key

question_en: Consider the linear programming problem: maximize \(c^T x\), subject to \(Ax=b\) and \(x\ge0\). Which statement is true?
question_gu: Consider the linear programming problem: maximize \(c^T x\), subject to \(Ax=b\) and \(x\ge0\). Which statement is true?
explanation_en: Feasibility requires both constraints simultaneously: Ax₀=b and x₀≥0. Either condition alone is insufficient. Even satisfying both only proves feasibility, not optimality, because the objective value must also be maximal. Therefore A, B and C are all false, so (D).
explanation_gu: Feasible solution માટે બંને શરતો સાથે જરૂરી છે: (Ax_0=b) અને (x_0\ge0). એકલી શરત પૂરતી નથી. બંને પૂરી થાય તો પણ માત્ર feasibility સાબિત થાય છે, optimality નહીં; objective maximum હોવું પણ જરૂરી છે. તેથી A, B, C ખોટાં અને (D) સાચું.
review_note: Answer checked against the repository's official GSET final answer-key transcription; question wording/options remain unverified against the original question paper.
tip_en: Separate feasibility (satisfying all constraints) from optimality (best objective value among feasible points).
tip_gu: Feasibility એટલે બધી constraints પૂરી કરવી; optimality એટલે feasible pointsમાં objectiveનું શ્રેષ્ઠ મૂલ્ય મેળવવું.
source: GSET official September 2013 Mathematical Sciences Paper-II question paper and corrected final answer key

question_en: Consider the linear programming problem: maximize \(3x_1+x_2\), subject to \(x_1+2x_2\le4\), \(6x_1+2x_2\le11\), \(x_1+x_2\le5\), and \(x_1,x_2\ge0\). Which statement is true?
question_gu: Consider the linear programming problem: maximize \(3x_1+x_2\), subject to \(x_1+2x_2\le4\), \(6x_1+2x_2\le11\), \(x_1+x_2\le5\), and \(x_1,x_2\ge0\). Which statement is true?
options_en: The L.P.P. has a unique optimum solution
The L.P.P. has two optimum solutions
The L.P.P. has infinitely many optimum solutions
The L.P.P. has no optimum solution
options_gu: The L.P.P. has a unique optimum solution
The L.P.P. has two optimum solutions
The L.P.P. has infinitely many optimum solutions
The L.P.P. has no optimum solution
explanation_en: The objective is 3x₁+x₂, and the second constraint is 6x₁+2x₂≤11, or 3x₁+x₂≤11/2. Thus the objective cannot exceed 11/2. The line 3x₁+x₂=11/2 contains a feasible segment: its endpoints satisfy the first constraint and non-negativity. Every point on that segment attains the same maximum 11/2, so there are infinitely many optimal solutions.
explanation_gu: Objective (3x_1+x_2) છે અને બીજી constraint (6x_1+2x_2\le11) એટલે (3x_1+x_2\le11/2). તેથી objective (11/2)થી મોટું ન થઈ શકે. (3x_1+x_2=11/2) રેખા પર feasible segment મળે છે, જેના બિંદુઓ non-negativity અને પહેલી constraint પણ પૂરી કરે છે. આ segmentના દરેક બિંદુએ સમાન maximum મળે છે; તેથી infinitely many optimal solutions છે.
review_note: Answer checked against the repository's official GSET final answer-key transcription; question wording/options remain unverified against the original question paper.
tip_en: If the objective function is parallel to a binding constraint, check whether a feasible segment gives multiple optima.
tip_gu: Objective function binding constraintને parallel હોય તો feasible segment પર multiple optimum solutions મળે છે કે નહીં તે તપાસો.
source: GSET official September 2013 Mathematical Sciences Paper-II question paper and corrected final answer key

question_en: Let \(\{a_n\}\) be a sequence of real numbers. Consider the statements: (i) \(\{a_n\}\) converges. (ii) \(\{a_{2n}\}\), \(\{a_{3n}\}\), and \(\{a_{2n+1}\}\) all converge. Then which of the following is true?
question_gu: \(\{a_n\}\) વાસ્તવિક સંખ્યાઓનો sequence છે. વિધાનો લો: (i) \(\{a_n\}\) converge થાય છે. (ii) \(\{a_{2n}\}\), \(\{a_{3n}\}\) અને \(\{a_{2n+1}\}\) બધા converge થાય છે. તો નીચેના પૈકી કયું સાચું છે?
explanation_en: If \(\{a_n\}\) converges, every subsequence listed in (ii) converges, so (i) implies (ii). Conversely, suppose \(\{a_{2n}\}\to L\), \(\{a_{2n+1}\}\to M\), and \(\{a_{3n}\}\) converges. The subsequence \(\{a_{6n}\}\) belongs to both \(\{a_{2n}\}\) and \(\{a_{3n}\}\), so the limit of \(\{a_{3n}\}\) is \(L\). The subsequence \(\{a_{6n+3}\}\) belongs to both \(\{a_{2n+1}\}\) and \(\{a_{3n}\}\), so that same limit is \(M\). Thus \(L=M\). The even and odd subsequences converge to the same limit, hence the full sequence converges. Therefore (ii) implies (i), and option (C) is correct.
explanation_gu: જો \(\{a_n\}\) converge થાય, તો તેની દરેક subsequence \(\{a_{2n}\}\), \(\{a_{3n}\}\), \(\{a_{2n+1}\}\) પણ converge થાય છે; એટલે (i)થી (ii) મળે છે. હવે \(\{a_{2n}\}\to L\), \(\{a_{2n+1}\}\to M\) અને \(\{a_{3n}\}\) converge થાય છે એમ માનો. \(\{a_{6n}\}\), even subsequence અને \(\{a_{3n}\}\) બંનેની subsequence હોવાથી \(\{a_{3n}\}\)નો limit \(L\) થાય છે. એ જ રીતે \(\{a_{6n+3}\}\) odd subsequence અને \(\{a_{3n}\}\) બંનેની subsequence હોવાથી એ limit \(M\) થાય છે. તેથી \(L=M\). Even અને odd subsequencesનો સમાન limit હોવાથી સંપૂર્ણ sequence converge થાય છે. એટલે (ii)થી (i) પણ મળે છે; વિકલ્પ (C) સાચો છે.
review_note: Question wording and all four implication options checked against official GSET September 2013 Paper-II PDF, printed page 12 (PDF page 12). Answer C matches the official corrected key. Answer checked against the repository's official GSET final answer-key transcription; question wording/options remain unverified against the original question paper.
tip_en: If the even and odd subsequences converge to the same limit, the entire sequence converges.
tip_gu: Even અને odd subsequencesનો limit સમાન હોય તો સંપૂર્ણ sequence converge થાય છે.
source: Official GSET Mathematical Sciences Paper-II, September 2013

question_en: Let \(A\) be the set of all polynomials with rational coefficients and \(B\) the set of all transcendental numbers. Which statement is true?
question_gu: Let \(A\) be the set of all polynomials with rational coefficients and \(B\) the set of all transcendental numbers. Which statement is true?
options_en: A is uncountable and B is countable
A is countable and B is uncountable
A is countable and B is countable
A is uncountable and B is uncountable
options_gu: A is uncountable and B is countable
A is countable and B is uncountable
A is countable and B is countable
A is uncountable and B is uncountable
explanation_en: Every polynomial has finite degree and finitely many rational coefficients. A countable union of countable sets is countable, so A is countable. The algebraic numbers are countable, while the real numbers are uncountable; therefore the transcendental numbers, the complement of the algebraic numbers in the reals, are uncountable. Option (B).
explanation_gu: દરેક polynomialની degree finite છે અને તેમાં rational coefficientsની finite યાદી હોય છે. Countable many finite-degree polynomial setsનો union countable છે, તેથી A countable છે. Algebraic numbers countable છે, જ્યારે real numbers uncountable છે; તેથી transcendental numbers uncountable છે. વિકલ્પ (B).
review_note: Answer checked against the repository's official GSET final answer-key transcription; question wording/options remain unverified against the original question paper.
tip_en: The set of polynomials over a countable field is countable; the set of real transcendental numbers is uncountable.
tip_gu: Countable field પરના polynomialsનો સમૂહ countable છે; real transcendental numbersનો સમૂહ uncountable છે.
source: GSET official September 2013 Mathematical Sciences Paper-II question paper and corrected final answer key

question_en: An example of a kernel function \(K(x,t)\) that is symmetric and separable is:
question_gu: An example of a kernel function \(K(x,t)\) that is symmetric and separable is:
explanation_en: A symmetric kernel satisfies K(x,t)=K(t,x), and a separable kernel can be expressed as a finite sum of products of a function of x and a function of t. Using the identity \(\sin(x^2+t^2)=\sin x^2\cos t^2+\cos x^2\sin t^2\), option (C) is symmetric and separable.
explanation_gu: Symmetric kernel માટે (K(x,t)=K(t,x)) અને separable kernel માટે x અને tના functionsના finite productsનો sum લખી શકાય. Identity (\sin(x^2+t^2)=\sin x^2\cos t^2+\cos x^2\sin t^2)થી વિકલ્પ (C) symmetric અને separable છે.
review_note: Answer checked against the repository's official GSET final answer-key transcription; question wording/options remain unverified against the original question paper.
tip_en: Use angle-addition identities to test whether a two-variable kernel can be separated into a finite sum of products.
tip_gu: Two-variable kernelને finite sum of productsમાં લખી શકાય છે કે નહીં તે માટે angle-addition identities વાપરો.
source: GSET official September 2013 Mathematical Sciences Paper-II question paper and corrected final answer key

question_en: Which of the following curves is characteristic for the first-order PDE \(y\frac{\partial u}{\partial x}-x\frac{\partial u}{\partial y}=0\)?
question_gu: First-order PDE \(y\frac{\partial u}{\partial x}-x\frac{\partial u}{\partial y}=0\) માટે નીચેની કઈ curve characteristic છે?
explanation_en: The characteristic equations are \(dx/ds=y\), \(dy/ds=-x\), and \(du/ds=0\). Along a characteristic, \(\frac{d}{ds}(x^2+y^2)=2x\frac{dx}{ds}+2y\frac{dy}{ds}=2xy-2xy=0\). Thus the characteristic curves satisfy \(x^2+y^2=C\), represented by option (B) in the printed options. However, the official corrected GSET answer key records option (C). The official key must remain authoritative, so the stored answer is retained as C and this source/key discrepancy is flagged for human review.
explanation_gu: Characteristic equations \(dx/ds=y\), \(dy/ds=-x\) અને \(du/ds=0\) છે. Characteristic પર \(\frac{d}{ds}(x^2+y^2)=2x\frac{dx}{ds}+2y\frac{dy}{ds}=2xy-2xy=0\), એટલે \(x^2+y^2=C\). આપેલા વિકલ્પોમાં આ વિકલ્પ (B) છે. પરંતુ GSETની સત્તાવાર corrected answer keyમાં વિકલ્પ (C) નોંધાયેલો છે. સત્તાવાર કી જ અધિકૃત હોવાથી stored answer C બદલ્યો નથી; આ key/question inconsistency માટે review જરૂરી છે.
review_note: Question wording and all four options checked against official GSET September 2013 Paper-II PDF, printed page 13 (PDF page 13). Mathematical characteristic curves give option B (x²+y²=C), but the official corrected answer key lists C. Keep official key C unchanged and resolve this source/key inconsistency by review. Answer checked against the repository's official GSET final answer-key transcription; question wording/options remain unverified against the original question paper.
tip_en: For first-order PDEs, derive characteristic curves from dx/P = dy/Q; compare with the official key.
tip_gu: First-order PDE માટે dx/P = dy/Q પરથી characteristic curves મેળવો; official key સાથે પણ સરખાવો.
source: Official GSET Mathematical Sciences Paper-II, September 2013

question_en: Let \(f(x)=x+\frac1x\), \(x>0\). Which of the following is true?
question_gu: Let \(f(x)=x+\frac1x\), \(x>0\). Which of the following is true?
options_en: f is unbounded and is not continuous at some points
f is bounded and \(0\le f(x)\le2\) for all x>0
f is bounded and \(2\le f(x)<\infty\) for all x>0
f is unbounded but continuous everywhere on its domain
options_gu: f is unbounded and is not continuous at some points
f is bounded and \(0\le f(x)\le2\) for all x>0
f is bounded and \(2\le f(x)<\infty\) for all x>0
f is unbounded but continuous everywhere on its domain
explanation_en: The function is continuous for every x>0 because it is a sum of continuous functions on that domain. As x→∞, f(x)→∞; as x→0⁺, 1/x→∞. Thus f is unbounded but continuous everywhere on its domain, option (D).
explanation_gu: (x>0) પર (x) અને (1/x) બંને continuous છે, તેથી તેમનો સરવાળો continuous છે. (x\to\infty) પર (f(x)\to\infty), અને (x\to0^+) પર (1/x\to\infty). તેથી function unbounded છે પરંતુ domainમાં દરેક જગ્યાએ continuous છે; વિકલ્પ (D).
review_note: Answer checked against the repository's official GSET final answer-key transcription; question wording/options remain unverified against the original question paper.
tip_en: Check continuity on the domain separately from boundedness at the domain's ends.
tip_gu: Domain પર continuity અને domainના છેડાઓ પાસે boundedness અલગથી તપાસો.
source: GSET official September 2013 Mathematical Sciences Paper-II question paper and corrected final answer key

question_en: Let \(S=\{(x_1,x_2,x_3)\in\mathbb R^3:x_1^2+x_2^2+x_3^2=1\}\) be the unit sphere and let A be a circle on S that does not contain \((0,0,1)\). What is the stereographic projection of A onto the complex plane?
question_gu: Let \(S=\{(x_1,x_2,x_3)\in\mathbb R^3:x_1^2+x_2^2+x_3^2=1\}\) be the unit sphere and let A be a circle on S that does not contain \((0,0,1)\). What is the stereographic projection of A onto the complex plane?
explanation_en: Stereographic projection maps a circle on the sphere that does not pass through the projection pole to a circle in the plane. A circle through the pole would project to a straight line; the stated circle avoids the pole, so its image is a circle, option (B).
explanation_gu: Stereographic projectionમાં sphere પરનો એવો circle જે projection poleમાંથી પસાર થતો નથી, તે planeમાં circleમાં map થાય છે. Poleમાંથી પસાર થતો circle straight lineમાં map થાય; અહીં circle poleથી દૂર છે, તેથી જવાબ (B).
review_note: Answer checked against the repository's official GSET final answer-key transcription; question wording/options remain unverified against the original question paper.
tip_en: Under stereographic projection, circles not through the projection pole map to circles; those through the pole map to lines.
tip_gu: Stereographic projectionમાં poleમાંથી ન પસાર થતો circle circleમાં અને poleમાંથી પસાર થતો circle lineમાં map થાય છે.
source: GSET official September 2013 Mathematical Sciences Paper-II question paper and corrected final answer key

question_en: The image of \(\{z\in\mathbb C:|\operatorname{Im}z|<\pi/2\}\) under the exponential map \(w=e^z\) is:
question_gu: The image of \(\{z\in\mathbb C:|\operatorname{Im}z|<\pi/2\}\) under the exponential map \(w=e^z\) is:
options_en: Interior of the upper half of the unit circle
Exterior of the upper half of the unit circle
options_gu: Interior of the upper half of the unit circle
Exterior of the upper half of the unit circle
explanation_en: Write z=x+iy with −π/2<y<π/2. Then w=eˣ(cos y+i sin y), so Re(w)=eˣ cos y>0 because cos y>0 on this interval. Every point in the right half-plane has an argument in this interval, so the image is the right half-plane.
explanation_gu: (z=x+iy), જ્યાં (-\pi/2<y<\pi/2). ત્યારે (w=e^x(\cos y+i\sin y)), એટલે (Re(w)=e^x\cos y>0), કારણ કે આ intervalમાં (cos y>0). Right half-planeના દરેક nonzero pointનો argument આ intervalમાં પસંદ કરી શકાય છે; તેથી image right half-plane છે.
review_note: Answer checked against the repository's official GSET final answer-key transcription; question wording/options remain unverified against the original question paper.
tip_en: For w=eᶻ, the real part of z controls the modulus and the imaginary part controls the argument.
tip_gu: (w=e^z)માં zનો real part modulus અને imaginary part argument નક્કી કરે છે.
source: GSET official September 2013 Mathematical Sciences Paper-II question paper and corrected final answer key

question_en: Which method gives the fastest approximation to the \(n\)-th root (\(n\in\mathbb N\)) of a given positive real number?
question_gu: Which method gives the fastest approximation to the \(n\)-th root (\(n\in\mathbb N\)) of a given positive real number?
explanation_en: Newton–Raphson iteration for solving f(x)=xⁿ−a=0 is \(x_{k+1}=x_k-\frac{x_k^n-a}{n x_k^{n-1}}=\frac1n((n-1)x_k+a/x_k^{n-1})\). Near a simple root it has quadratic convergence, generally faster than the linear convergence of bisection and Regula-Falsi.
explanation_gu: (n)મો root મેળવવા (f(x)=x^n-a=0) માટે Newton–Raphson iteration (x_{k+1}=x_k-\frac{x_k^n-a}{n x_k^{n-1}}=\frac1n((n-1)x_k+a/x_k^{n-1})) છે. Simple root પાસે તેની quadratic convergence હોય છે, જે સામાન્ય રીતે bisection અને Regula-Falsiની linear convergence કરતાં ઝડપી છે.
review_note: Answer checked against the repository's official GSET final answer-key transcription; question wording/options remain unverified against the original question paper.
tip_en: Newton–Raphson usually converges quadratically near a simple root when the starting value is suitable.
tip_gu: યોગ્ય initial value હોય તો simple root પાસે Newton–Raphson સામાન્ય રીતે quadratic convergence આપે છે.
source: GSET official September 2013 Mathematical Sciences Paper-II question paper and corrected final answer key

question_en: If the Lagrangian of a dynamical system with generalized coordinates x and y is \(L(x,y,\dot x,\dot y,t)=\frac12(\dot x^2-2\dot x\dot y+\dot y^2)+5xy\), then one of Lagrange's equations is:
question_gu: If the Lagrangian of a dynamical system with generalized coordinates x and y is \(L(x,y,\dot x,\dot y,t)=\frac12(\dot x^2-2\dot x\dot y+\dot y^2)+5xy\), then one of Lagrange's equations is:
explanation_en: For coordinate x, Lagrange's equation is d/dt(∂L/∂ẋ)−∂L/∂x=0. Here ∂L/∂ẋ=ẋ−ẏ, so d/dt gives ẍ−ÿ; also ∂L/∂x=5y. Therefore ẍ−ÿ−5y=0, option (C).
explanation_gu: Coordinate x માટે (\frac{d}{dt}(\frac{\partial L}{\partial\dot x})-\frac{\partial L}{\partial x}=0). અહીં (\frac{\partial L}{\partial\dot x}=\dot x-\dot y), તેથી time derivative (\ddot x-\ddot y); અને (\frac{\partial L}{\partial x}=5y). એટલે (\ddot x-\ddot y-5y=0), વિકલ્પ (C).
review_note: Answer checked against the repository's official GSET final answer-key transcription; question wording/options remain unverified against the original question paper.
tip_en: Apply the Euler–Lagrange equation to one generalized coordinate at a time.
tip_gu: Euler–Lagrange equation દરેક generalized coordinate માટે અલગથી લાગુ કરો.
source: GSET official September 2013 Mathematical Sciences Paper-II question paper and corrected final answer key

question_en: For a conservative dynamical system whose geometrical equations do not contain time explicitly, and where L, T and V denote the Lagrangian, kinetic energy and potential energy respectively, which quantity is constant?
question_gu: For a conservative dynamical system whose geometrical equations do not contain time explicitly, and where L, T and V denote the Lagrangian, kinetic energy and potential energy respectively, which quantity is constant?
explanation_en: For a conservative system with no explicit time dependence, the conserved mechanical energy is E=T+V. Since L=T−V, the conserved quantity is T+V, option (C).
explanation_gu: Explicit time dependence ન ધરાવતા conservative systemમાં conserved mechanical energy (E=T+V) છે. કારણ કે (L=T-V), conserved quantity (T+V) છે; વિકલ્પ (C).
review_note: Answer checked against the repository's official GSET final answer-key transcription; question wording/options remain unverified against the original question paper.
tip_en: For a time-independent conservative Lagrangian, the conserved energy is kinetic plus potential energy.
tip_gu: Time-independent conservative Lagrangian માટે conserved energy kinetic energy અને potential energyનો સરવાળો છે.
source: GSET official September 2013 Mathematical Sciences Paper-II question paper and corrected final answer key

question_en: Let G be a group of order 15 and H a proper subgroup of G. Which statement is true?
question_gu: Let G be a group of order 15 and H a proper subgroup of G. Which statement is true?
options_en: H must be a cyclic group
H must be abelian but need not be cyclic
H may not be abelian but it must be cyclic
H may be neither abelian nor cyclic
options_gu: H must be a cyclic group
H must be abelian but need not be cyclic
H may not be abelian but it must be cyclic
H may be neither abelian nor cyclic
explanation_en: By Lagrange's theorem, the order of H divides 15. Since H is a proper subgroup, |H| is 1, 3 or 5. Groups of prime order are cyclic, and the trivial group is also cyclic. Hence H must be cyclic, option (A).
explanation_gu: Lagrange theorem પ્રમાણે (|H|), 15ને divide કરે છે. H proper હોવાથી (|H|=1,3) અથવા 5. Prime order ધરાવતા groups cyclic હોય છે અને trivial group પણ cyclic ગણાય છે. તેથી H cyclic હોવો જ જોઈએ; વિકલ્પ (A).
review_note: Answer checked against the repository's official GSET final answer-key transcription; question wording/options remain unverified against the original question paper.
tip_en: Use Lagrange's theorem to list the possible subgroup orders, then classify groups of prime order.
tip_gu: Lagrange theoremથી subgroupના શક્ય orders કાઢો, પછી prime order groups cyclic હોય છે તે વાપરો.
source: GSET official September 2013 Mathematical Sciences Paper-II question paper and corrected final answer key

question_en: If N is a normal subgroup of G, which statement is false?
question_gu: If N is a normal subgroup of G, which statement is false?
options_en: Every left coset of N in G is a right coset of N in G
The product of any two right cosets of N in G is again a right coset of N in G
N must be a cyclic subgroup of G
options_gu: Every left coset of N in G is a right coset of N in G
The product of any two right cosets of N in G is again a right coset of N in G
N must be a cyclic subgroup of G
explanation_en: Normality means gNg⁻¹=N for every g∈G, and it ensures each left coset is also a right coset. Coset multiplication is well-defined in the quotient group G/N, so a product of two cosets is a coset. A normal subgroup need not be cyclic; therefore (D) is false.
explanation_gu: Normal subgroup માટે દરેક (g\in G) માટે (gNg^{-1}=N) થાય છે અને દરેક left coset એક right coset પણ છે. Quotient group (G/N)માં coset multiplication well-defined છે, તેથી બે cosetsનો product coset છે. પરંતુ normal subgroup cyclic હોવો જરૂરી નથી; તેથી (D) ખોટું છે.
review_note: Answer checked against the repository's official GSET final answer-key transcription; question wording/options remain unverified against the original question paper.
tip_en: Normality controls conjugation and left/right cosets; it does not imply the subgroup is cyclic.
tip_gu: Normality conjugation અને left/right cosets વિશે છે; તે subgroup cyclic હોવાની ખાતરી આપતી નથી.
source: GSET official September 2013 Mathematical Sciences Paper-II question paper and corrected final answer key

question_en: Let \(J(\sqrt2)=\{m+n\sqrt2:m,n\in\mathbb Z\}\), and define \(\phi:J(\sqrt2)\to J(\sqrt2)\) by \(\phi(m+n\sqrt2)=m-n\sqrt2\). Which statement is true?
question_gu: Let \(J(\sqrt2)=\{m+n\sqrt2:m,n\in\mathbb Z\}\), and define \(\phi:J(\sqrt2)\to J(\sqrt2)\) by \(\phi(m+n\sqrt2)=m-n\sqrt2\). Which statement is true?
options_en: \(J(\sqrt2)\) is not a group under usual addition of real numbers
\(J(\sqrt2)\) is a ring and \(\phi\) is not a ring homomorphism
\(J(\sqrt2)\) is a group under addition but is not a ring
\(J(\sqrt2)\) is a ring and \(\phi\) is a ring homomorphism
options_gu: \(J(\sqrt2)\) is not a group under usual addition of real numbers
\(J(\sqrt2)\) is a ring and \(\phi\) is not a ring homomorphism
\(J(\sqrt2)\) is a group under addition but is not a ring
\(J(\sqrt2)\) is a ring and \(\phi\) is a ring homomorphism
explanation_en: The set is closed under addition, subtraction and multiplication because \((m+n\sqrt2)(p+q\sqrt2)=(mp+2nq)+(mq+np)\sqrt2\), so it is a ring. The map φ is conjugation: it preserves addition and multiplication, since φ(ab)=φ(a)φ(b). Hence it is a ring homomorphism, option (D).
explanation_gu: આ set addition, subtraction અને multiplication હેઠળ closed છે, કારણ કે ((m+n\sqrt2)(p+q\sqrt2)=(mp+2nq)+(mq+np)\sqrt2); તેથી તે ring છે. (phi) conjugation છે અને addition તથા multiplication જાળવે છે: (phi(ab)=phi(a)phi(b)). તેથી ring homomorphism છે; વિકલ્પ (D).
review_note: Answer checked against the repository's official GSET final answer-key transcription; question wording/options remain unverified against the original question paper.
tip_en: Check closure under multiplication and whether the map preserves both addition and multiplication.
tip_gu: Multiplication હેઠળ closure અને map addition તથા multiplication બંને જાળવે છે કે નહીં તે તપાસો.
source: GSET official September 2013 Mathematical Sciences Paper-II question paper and corrected final answer key

question_en: Let E be the set of all even integers with usual addition and multiplication. Which statement is false?
question_gu: Let E be the set of all even integers with usual addition and multiplication. Which statement is false?
options_en: E is an ideal of the ring of all integers
options_gu: E is an ideal of the ring of all integers
explanation_en: The even integers form a commutative ring without zero divisors, so they are an integral domain under the usual non-unital convention. They form the ideal 2ℤ of ℤ. But E is not a field: for example, 2 has no multiplicative inverse in E. Thus (C) is false.
explanation_gu: Even integers addition અને multiplication હેઠળ commutative ring છે અને તેમાં zero divisors નથી. તે (mathbb Z)નો ideal (2mathbb Z) પણ છે. પરંતુ E field નથી, કારણ કે 2નો multiplicative inverse Eમાં નથી. તેથી (C) ખોટું છે.
review_note: Answer checked against the repository's official GSET final answer-key transcription; question wording/options remain unverified against the original question paper.
tip_en: A field requires every nonzero element to have a multiplicative inverse in the set.
tip_gu: Fieldમાં દરેક nonzero elementનો multiplicative inverse એ જ setમાં હોવો જોઈએ.
source: GSET official September 2013 Mathematical Sciences Paper-II question paper and corrected final answer key

question_en: Let \(S_1=\{(x,y,z)\in\mathbb R^3:2x-y+3z=5\}\) and \(S_2=\{(x,y,z)\in\mathbb R^3:x+y+z=0,\;7x-5y-2z=0\}\). Which statement is true?
question_gu: Let \(S_1=\{(x,y,z)\in\mathbb R^3:2x-y+3z=5\}\) and \(S_2=\{(x,y,z)\in\mathbb R^3:x+y+z=0,\;7x-5y-2z=0\}\). Which statement is true?
options_en: \(S_1\) is a two-dimensional linear subspace of \(\mathbb R^3\), whereas \(S_2\) is a one-dimensional linear subspace
\(S_1\) is not a linear subspace and \(S_2\) is a two-dimensional linear subspace
\(S_1\) is not a linear subspace and \(S_2\) is a one-dimensional linear subspace
Both \(S_1\) and \(S_2\) are one-dimensional linear subspaces
options_gu: \(S_1\) is a two-dimensional linear subspace of \(\mathbb R^3\), whereas \(S_2\) is a one-dimensional linear subspace
\(S_1\) is not a linear subspace and \(S_2\) is a two-dimensional linear subspace
\(S_1\) is not a linear subspace and \(S_2\) is a one-dimensional linear subspace
Both \(S_1\) and \(S_2\) are one-dimensional linear subspaces
explanation_en: The set S₁ is an affine plane that does not contain the origin because its equation has right-hand side 5; therefore it is not a linear subspace. S₂ is the solution space of two independent homogeneous linear equations in ℝ³, so its dimension is 3−2=1. Option (C).
explanation_gu: (S_1)નું સમીકરણ (2x-y+3z=5) છે, એટલે તે originમાંથી પસાર થતું નથી અને linear subspace નથી. (S_2) એ (mathbb R^3)માં બે independent homogeneous linear equationsનું solution space છે; તેની dimension (3-2=1) છે. તેથી (C).
review_note: Answer checked against the repository's official GSET final answer-key transcription; question wording/options remain unverified against the original question paper.
tip_en: A linear subspace must contain the origin; independent homogeneous constraints reduce dimension by their rank.
tip_gu: Linear subspaceમાં origin હોવો જરૂરી છે; independent homogeneous constraints dimension ઘટાડે છે.
source: GSET official September 2013 Mathematical Sciences Paper-II question paper and corrected final answer key

question_en: Let \(T:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^3\) be defined by \(T(x,y,z)=(x-y,\;y-z,\;z-x)\). Which statement is true?
question_gu: Let \(T:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^3\) be defined by \(T(x,y,z)=(x-y,\;y-z,\;z-x)\). Which statement is true?
options_en: T is linear but not one-to-one
T is one-to-one but not linear
T is neither one-to-one nor linear
options_gu: T is linear but not one-to-one
T is one-to-one but not linear
T is neither one-to-one nor linear
explanation_en: Each component is linear, so T is a linear transformation. But T(x,y,z)=(0,0,0) whenever x=y=z, so the kernel contains all vectors (t,t,t), not just the zero vector. Thus T is not one-to-one; option (B).
explanation_gu: દરેક component linear છે, તેથી T linear transformation છે. પરંતુ (T(t,t,t)=(0,0,0)) દરેક t માટે, એટલે kernelમાં zero સિવાય પણ vectors છે. તેથી T one-to-one નથી; વિકલ્પ (B).
review_note: Answer checked against the repository's official GSET final answer-key transcription; question wording/options remain unverified against the original question paper.
tip_en: A linear transformation is injective exactly when its kernel contains only the zero vector.
tip_gu: Linear transformation one-to-one ત્યારે જ હોય જ્યારે તેનું kernel માત્ર zero vector ધરાવે.
source: GSET official September 2013 Mathematical Sciences Paper-II question paper and corrected final answer key

question_en: Let T be a linear transformation from a linear space X to a linear space Y, with range M and null space N. Which statement is true?
question_gu: Let T be a linear transformation from a linear space X to a linear space Y, with range M and null space N. Which statement is true?
options_en: Both M and N must be finite-dimensional linear subspaces
If M is finite-dimensional, N must be infinite-dimensional
If N is finite-dimensional, M must be infinite-dimensional
Both M and N may be infinite-dimensional linear subspaces
options_gu: Both M and N must be finite-dimensional linear subspaces
If M is finite-dimensional, N must be infinite-dimensional
If N is finite-dimensional, M must be infinite-dimensional
Both M and N may be infinite-dimensional linear subspaces
explanation_en: The range and null space are linear subspaces, and both can be infinite-dimensional. For example, on an infinite-dimensional vector space with basis split into two infinite subsets, define T to map one subset to a basis for an infinite-dimensional range and send the other subset to zero. Then both range and null space are infinite-dimensional. Thus (D).
explanation_gu: Range અને null space બંને linear subspaces છે અને બંને infinite-dimensional હોઈ શકે. ઉદાહરણ તરીકે, infinite-dimensional basisને બે infinite subsetsમાં વહેંચીને એક subsetને infinite-dimensional rangeના basis પર map કરો અને બીજા subsetને zero પર મોકલો. ત્યારે range અને null space બંને infinite-dimensional થાય છે. તેથી (D).
review_note: Answer checked against the repository's official GSET final answer-key transcription; question wording/options remain unverified against the original question paper.
tip_en: Do not assume the range and kernel must have the same finite/infinite dimensionality; construct examples using a basis.
tip_gu: Range અને kernelની dimension હંમેશા સમાન પ્રકારની જ હોય એવું માનશો નહીં; basisથી example બનાવી શકાય.
source: GSET official September 2013 Mathematical Sciences Paper-II question paper and corrected final answer key

question_en: The Euler–Lagrange condition for an extremal of the functional \(\int_a^b F(x,y,y')\,dx\) is:
question_gu: The Euler–Lagrange condition for an extremal of the functional \(\int_a^b F(x,y,y')\,dx\) is:
explanation_en: The Euler–Lagrange equation is \(\frac{\partial F}{\partial y}-\frac{d}{dx}\left(\frac{\partial F}{\partial y'}\right)=0\). Rearranging gives \(F_y=\frac{d}{dx}(F_{y'})\), option (A).
explanation_gu: Euler–Lagrange equation (\frac{\partial F}{\partial y}-\frac{d}{dx}(\frac{\partial F}{\partial y'})=0) છે. Rearranging કરતાં (F_y=\frac{d}{dx}(F_{y'})) મળે છે; વિકલ્પ (A).
review_note: Answer checked against the repository's official GSET final answer-key transcription; question wording/options remain unverified against the original question paper.
tip_en: For a functional depending on y and y′, differentiate F with respect to y and take the total x-derivative of F with respect to y′.
tip_gu: y અને y′ પર આધારિત functional માટે Fને y પ્રમાણે differentiate કરો અને Fના y′ derivativeનો total x-derivative લો.
source: GSET official September 2013 Mathematical Sciences Paper-II question paper and corrected final answer key

question_en: Let \(y(x)\) solve \(\frac{d^2y}{dx^2}+3\frac{dy}{dx}+2y=\sin x\), for \(x\in\mathbb R\). Then \(\lim_{x\to\infty}y(x)\):
question_gu: Let \(y(x)\) solve \(\frac{d^2y}{dx^2}+3\frac{dy}{dx}+2y=\sin x\), for \(x\in\mathbb R\). Then \(\lim_{x\to\infty}y(x)\):
explanation_en: The homogeneous solution is \(C_1e^{-x}+C_2e^{-2x}\), which tends to zero as x→∞. A particular solution for the sinusoidal forcing is a nonzero combination of sin x and cos x, which continues to oscillate. Hence the full solution has no limit as x→∞.
explanation_gu: Homogeneous solution (C_1e^{-x}+C_2e^{-2x}) છે, જે (x\to\infty) પર zero થાય છે. પરંતુ (sin x) forcing માટે particular solution nonzero sin અને cosના combination રૂપે મળે છે, જે સતત oscillate કરે છે. તેથી (y(x))નો limit અસ્તિત્વમાં નથી.
review_note: Answer checked against the repository's official GSET final answer-key transcription; question wording/options remain unverified against the original question paper.
tip_en: A decaying transient plus a persistent sinusoidal particular solution has no finite limit.
tip_gu: Decay થતો transient અને સતત oscillate થતો particular solution હોય તો finite limit મળતો નથી.
source: GSET official September 2013 Mathematical Sciences Paper-II question paper and corrected final answer key

question_en: Consider \(y'=y^2-1\), \(x>0\), with initial condition \(y(0)=y_0\). For \(-1<y_0<1\), which statement is true?
question_gu: Consider \(y'=y^2-1\), \(x>0\), with initial condition \(y(0)=y_0\). For \(-1<y_0<1\), which statement is true?
options_en: The graph of y(x) is concave downwards
The graph of y(x) is concave upwards
options_gu: The graph of y(x) is concave downwards
The graph of y(x) is concave upwards
explanation_en: When −1<y<1, y′=y²−1<0, so the solution decreases. The equilibrium y=−1 is approached as x increases; solving by separation gives a solution that tends to −1 as x→∞. Hence (B).
explanation_gu: (-1<y<1) હોય ત્યારે (y'=y^2-1<0), એટલે solution ઘટે છે. Separation of variablesથી મળતો solution x વધતાં equilibrium (y=-1) તરફ જાય છે. તેથી (x\to\infty) પર (y\to-1), વિકલ્પ (B).
review_note: Answer checked against the repository's official GSET final answer-key transcription; question wording/options remain unverified against the original question paper.
tip_en: For autonomous first-order ODEs, inspect the sign of y′ between equilibrium solutions.
tip_gu: Autonomous first-order ODEમાં equilibrium solutions વચ્ચે y′ની sign તપાસો.
source: GSET official September 2013 Mathematical Sciences Paper-II question paper and corrected final answer key

question_en: What is the singular solution of \(\left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right)^2+x\frac{dy}{dx}-y=0\)?
question_gu: What is the singular solution of \(\left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right)^2+x\frac{dy}{dx}-y=0\)?
explanation_en: Let p=dy/dx. The equation gives y=xp+p², a Clairaut equation. Its general solution is y=Cx+C². The singular solution is the envelope found from ∂y/∂C=x+2C=0, so C=−x/2. Substituting gives y=−x²/4, or x²+4y=0.
explanation_gu: (p=dy/dx) લો. સમીકરણ (y=xp+p^2) આપે છે, જે Clairaut equation છે. General solution (y=Cx+C^2) છે. Singular solution માટે envelope condition (\partial y/\partial C=x+2C=0), એટલે (C=-x/2). Substitute કરતાં (y=-x^2/4), એટલે (x^2+4y=0).
review_note: Answer checked against the repository's official GSET final answer-key transcription; question wording/options remain unverified against the original question paper.
tip_en: For a Clairaut equation, obtain the singular solution by taking the envelope of the one-parameter family.
tip_gu: Clairaut equationમાં one-parameter familyનો envelope લઈને singular solution મેળવો.
source: GSET official September 2013 Mathematical Sciences Paper-II question paper and corrected final answer key

question_en: The relation \(F(x,y,z,a,b)=0\), where a and b are constants, satisfies a first-order PDE \(f\!\left(x,y,z,\frac{\partial z}{\partial x},\frac{\partial z}{\partial y}\right)=0\). It represents the:
question_gu: The relation \(F(x,y,z,a,b)=0\), where a and b are constants, satisfies a first-order PDE \(f\!\left(x,y,z,\frac{\partial z}{\partial x},\frac{\partial z}{\partial y}\right)=0\). It represents the:
explanation_en: A complete integral of a first-order PDE contains as many independent arbitrary constants as the number of independent variables (two constants for z(x,y), under the standard first-order complete-integral definition). Therefore the two-parameter family F(x,y,z,a,b)=0 is a complete integral, option (C).
explanation_gu: First-order PDE (z(x,y)) માટે standard complete integralમાં બે independent arbitrary constants હોય છે. (F(x,y,z,a,b)=0) બે constants a અને b ધરાવતી family છે, તેથી તે complete integral છે; વિકલ્પ (C).
review_note: Answer checked against the repository's official GSET final answer-key transcription; question wording/options remain unverified against the original question paper.
tip_en: For a first-order PDE in two independent variables, a complete integral generally contains two independent arbitrary constants.
tip_gu: બે independent variables ધરાવતી first-order PDEના complete integralમાં સામાન્ય રીતે બે independent arbitrary constants હોય છે.
source: GSET official September 2013 Mathematical Sciences Paper-II question paper and corrected final answer key

question_en: For points \((x,y)\) in the region \(-1<y<1\), \(0<x<2\), the equation \((y^2-1)u_{xx}+2xu_{xy}-u_{yy}=x+y\) is parabolic on a:
question_gu: For points \((x,y)\) in the region \(-1<y<1\), \(0<x<2\), the equation \((y^2-1)u_{xx}+2xu_{xy}-u_{yy}=x+y\) is parabolic on a:
explanation_en: For a second-order PDE A uₓₓ+2B uₓᵧ+C uᵧᵧ=…, the parabolic condition is B²−AC=0. Here A=y²−1, B=x and C=−1, so B²−AC=x²+y²−1. The parabolic locus is x²+y²=1, a circle, option (D).
explanation_gu: Second-order PDE (Au_{xx}+2Bu_{xy}+Cu_{yy}=\cdots) parabolic ત્યારે હોય જ્યારે (B^2-AC=0). અહીં (A=y^2-1), (B=x), (C=-1), એટલે (B^2-AC=x^2+y^2-1). તેથી locus (x^2+y^2=1), એટલે circle; વિકલ્પ (D).
review_note: Answer checked against the repository's official GSET final answer-key transcription; question wording/options remain unverified against the original question paper.
tip_en: Classify a second-order PDE using the discriminant B²−AC.
tip_gu: Second-order PDEનું classification કરવા discriminant (B^2-AC) વાપરો.
source: GSET official September 2013 Mathematical Sciences Paper-II question paper and corrected final answer key

question_en: Which relation is implied by the characteristic equations of the differential equation \(z=pq\), where \(p=\frac{\partial z}{\partial x}\) and \(q=\frac{\partial z}{\partial y}\)? Here a is an arbitrary constant.
question_gu: Which relation is implied by the characteristic equations of the differential equation \(z=pq\), where \(p=\frac{\partial z}{\partial x}\) and \(q=\frac{\partial z}{\partial y}\)? Here a is an arbitrary constant.
explanation_en: For the first-order PDE F=z−pq=0, Charpit's equations give dp/ds=−p and dq/ds=−q. Therefore d(p/q)/ds=0, so p/q is constant along characteristics. Writing that constant as a gives p=aq, option (C).
explanation_gu: First-order PDE (F=z-pq=0) માટે Charpit equations (dp/ds=-p) અને (dq/ds=-q) આપે છે. તેથી (p/q) characteristics પર constant રહે છે. આ constantને a માનતાં (p=aq) મળે છે; વિકલ્પ (C).
review_note: Answer checked against the repository's official GSET final answer-key transcription; question wording/options remain unverified against the original question paper.
tip_en: Use Charpit's equations to find quantities that remain constant along characteristics.
tip_gu: Characteristics પર કઈ quantity constant રહે છે તે શોધવા Charpit equations વાપરો.
source: GSET official September 2013 Mathematical Sciences Paper-II question paper and corrected final answer key

question_en: In a survey of 20 observations on X, the data summaries were \(\sum x_i=100\) and \(\sum x_i^2=1000\). Two observations were corrected: one had been recorded as 10 instead of 11, and another as 10 instead of 9. By what amount does \(s^2=\frac1n\sum(x_i-\bar x)^2\) increase after correction?
question_gu: In a survey of 20 observations on X, the data summaries were \(\sum x_i=100\) and \(\sum x_i^2=1000\). Two observations were corrected: one had been recorded as 10 instead of 11, and another as 10 instead of 9. By what amount does \(s^2=\frac1n\sum(x_i-\bar x)^2\) increase after correction?
explanation_en: The corrections change the sum by (11−10)+(9−10)=0, so the mean remains 100/20=5. The sum of squares increases by (11²−10²)+(9²−10²)=21−19=2. Since \(s^2=\sum x_i^2/n-\bar x^2\), the increase is 2/20=0.1.
review_note: Answer checked against the repository's official GSET final answer-key transcription; question wording/options remain unverified against the original question paper.
tip_en: When the mean stays fixed, the change in this variance definition is the change in Σxᵢ² divided by n.
tip_gu: Mean અચળ રહે ત્યારે varianceમાં ફેરફાર, (sum x_i^2)ના ફેરફારને nથી ભાગ્યા બરાબર છે.
source: GSET official September 2013 Mathematical Sciences Paper-II question paper and corrected final answer key

question_en: Let \((x_i,y_i), i=1,2,\ldots,n\), be pairs of observations and fit the no-intercept model \(y=\beta x+\varepsilon\). Let \(\hat\beta\) be the least-squares estimate and \(\hat y_i=\hat\beta x_i\). Which of the following equations hold? (1) \(\hat\beta=\frac{\sum x_i y_i}{\sum x_i^2}\); (2) \(\hat\beta=\frac{\sum(x_i-\bar x)(y_i-\bar y)}{\sum(x_i-\bar x)^2}\); (3) \(\sum y_i=\sum\hat y_i\).
question_gu: Let \((x_i,y_i), i=1,2,\ldots,n\), be pairs of observations and fit the no-intercept model \(y=\beta x+\varepsilon\). Let \(\hat\beta\) be the least-squares estimate and \(\hat y_i=\hat\beta x_i\). Which of the following equations hold? (1) \(\hat\beta=\frac{\sum x_i y_i}{\sum x_i^2}\); (2) \(\hat\beta=\frac{\sum(x_i-\bar x)(y_i-\bar y)}{\sum(x_i-\bar x)^2}\); (3) \(\sum y_i=\sum\hat y_i\).
explanation_en: For least squares through the origin, minimize Σ(yᵢ−βxᵢ)². Differentiating with respect to β and setting to zero gives \(\hat\beta=\sum x_i y_i/\sum x_i^2\), so (1) holds. Formula (2) is the usual slope when an intercept is fitted, not the no-intercept model. The normal equation gives Σxᵢ(yᵢ−ŷᵢ)=0, not generally Σyᵢ=Σŷᵢ, so (3) need not hold. Answer (A).
explanation_gu: Originમાંથી પસાર થતી least-squares line માટે (sum(y_i- eta x_i)^2) minimize કરીએ. ( eta) પ્રમાણે differentiate કરીને zero મૂકતાં (hat\beta=\sum x_i y_i/\sum x_i^2) મળે છે; એટલે (1) સાચું. (2) intercept ધરાવતી regression lineનું slope છે. Normal equation (sum x_i(y_i-hat y_i)=0) આપે છે, પરંતુ સામાન્ય રીતે (sum y_i=sumhat y_i) નહીં; એટલે (3) જરૂરી નથી. જવાબ (A).
review_note: Answer checked against the repository's official GSET final answer-key transcription; question wording/options remain unverified against the original question paper.
tip_en: Regression through the origin uses Σxy/Σx²; do not substitute the centered slope formula from a model with an intercept.
tip_gu: Originમાંથી પસાર થતી regression માટે (sum xy/sum x^2) વાપરો; intercept ધરાવતા modelનું centered slope formula અહીં લાગુ પડતું નથી.
source: GSET official September 2013 Mathematical Sciences Paper-II question paper and corrected final answer key

question_en: If \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\) are i.i.d. random variables with \(E(X_1)=\mu\) and \(V(X_1)=\sigma^2\), then which of the following is correct?
question_gu: જો \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\) i.i.d. random variables હોય અને \(E(X_1)=\mu\), \(V(X_1)=\sigma^2\) હોય, તો નીચેના પૈકી કયું સાચું છે?
explanation_en: Since the variables are i.i.d., \(E(\bar X)=\mu\) and \(\operatorname{Var}(\bar X)=\sigma^2/n\). Chebyshev's inequality gives \(P(|\bar X-\mu|\ge t)\le \operatorname{Var}(\bar X)/t^2\). Set \(t=c\sigma/\sqrt n\): \(P(|\bar X-\mu|\ge c\sigma/\sqrt n)\le(\sigma^2/n)/(c^2\sigma^2/n)=1/c^2\). This is option (B).
explanation_gu: Variables i.i.d. હોવાથી \(E(\bar X)=\mu\) અને \(\operatorname{Var}(\bar X)=\sigma^2/n\). Chebyshev inequality મુજબ \(P(|\bar X-\mu|\ge t)\le\operatorname{Var}(\bar X)/t^2\). \(t=c\sigma/\sqrt n\) મૂક્તાં \(P(|\bar X-\mu|\ge c\sigma/\sqrt n)\le(\sigma^2/n)/(c^2\sigma^2/n)=1/c^2\). તેથી વિકલ્પ (B) સાચો છે.
review_note: Question wording and all four mathematical options checked against official GSET September 2013 Paper-II PDF, printed page 21 (PDF page 21). Answer B matches the official corrected key. Answer checked against the repository's official GSET final answer-key transcription; question wording/options remain unverified against the original question paper.
tip_en: For the sample mean, Var(X̄) = σ²/n; then apply Chebyshev's inequality.
tip_gu: Sample mean માટે Var(X̄) = σ²/n લઈને Chebyshev inequality વાપરો.
source: Official GSET Mathematical Sciences Paper-II, September 2013

question_en: Let X and Y be independent random variables. What is the characteristic function of \(X-Y\)?
question_gu: Let X and Y be independent random variables. What is the characteristic function of \(X-Y\)?
explanation_en: By definition, \(\phi_{X-Y}(t)=E[e^{it(X-Y)}]=E[e^{itX}e^{-itY}]\). Independence factors the expectation, giving \(E[e^{itX}]E[e^{-itY}]=\phi_X(t)\phi_Y(-t)\), option (D).
explanation_gu: Definition પ્રમાણે (phi_{X-Y}(t)=E[e^{it(X-Y)}]=E[e^{itX}e^{-itY}]). Independenceથી expectation factor થાય છે: (E[e^{itX}]E[e^{-itY}]=phi_X(t)phi_Y(-t)). તેથી (D).
review_note: Answer checked against the repository's official GSET final answer-key transcription; question wording/options remain unverified against the original question paper.
tip_en: For a difference, replace t by −t in the second variable's characteristic function.
tip_gu: Difference માટે બીજા variableના characteristic functionમાં tના બદલે −t મૂકો.
source: GSET official September 2013 Mathematical Sciences Paper-II question paper and corrected final answer key

question_en: If \(X_n\xrightarrow{d}X\) and \(Y_n\xrightarrow{d}Y\), which is an appropriate condition to ensure \(X_n+Y_n\xrightarrow{d}X+Y\)?
question_gu: If \(X_n\xrightarrow{d}X\) and \(Y_n\xrightarrow{d}Y\), which is an appropriate condition to ensure \(X_n+Y_n\xrightarrow{d}X+Y\)?
options_en: \(X_n\) and \(Y_n\) are independent for every n
Both X and Y are degenerate
options_gu: \(X_n\) and \(Y_n\) are independent for every n
Both X and Y are degenerate
explanation_en: Marginal convergence alone does not generally imply convergence of the sum. If Xₙ and Yₙ are independent for every n, their joint distributions converge to the product distribution of independent limits X and Y. The continuous mapping theorem applied to (x,y)↦x+y then gives convergence in distribution of the sums. Option (A).
explanation_gu: માત્ર marginal convergenceથી sumની convergence સામાન્ય રીતે નક્કી થતી નથી. દરેક n માટે (X_n) અને (Y_n) independent હોય તો joint distribution independent limits (X,Y)ના product distribution તરફ converge થાય છે. પછી continuous mapping theoremથી (X_n+Y_n\xrightarrow{d}X+Y). વિકલ્પ (A).
review_note: Answer checked against the repository's official GSET final answer-key transcription; question wording/options remain unverified against the original question paper.
tip_en: For sums of random variables, check joint convergence; independence for each n is a standard sufficient condition.
tip_gu: Random variablesના sum માટે joint convergence તપાસો; દરેક n પર independence એક standard sufficient condition છે.
source: GSET official September 2013 Mathematical Sciences Paper-II question paper and corrected final answer key

question_en: Let \((X,Y)\) have joint distribution function \(F(x,y)\). Then what is \(P(X>x;\,Y>y)\)?
question_gu: જો \((X,Y)\)નું joint distribution function \(F(x,y)\) હોય, તો \(P(X>x;\,Y>y)\) કેટલું છે?
explanation_en: Use the complement and inclusion-exclusion. \(P(X>x,Y>y)=1-P(X\le x\ \text{or}\ Y\le y)\). Also \(P(X\le x)=F_X(x)\), \(P(Y\le y)=F_Y(y)\), and \(P(X\le x,Y\le y)=F(x,y)\). Therefore \(P(X>x,Y>y)=1-F_X(x)-F_Y(y)+F(x,y)\), option (D).
explanation_gu: Complement અને inclusion-exclusion વાપરો: \(P(X>x,Y>y)=1-P(X\le x\ \text{or}\ Y\le y)\). અહીં \(P(X\le x)=F_X(x)\), \(P(Y\le y)=F_Y(y)\), અને \(P(X\le x,Y\le y)=F(x,y)\). તેથી \(P(X>x,Y>y)=1-F_X(x)-F_Y(y)+F(x,y)\), એટલે વિકલ્પ (D) સાચો છે.
review_note: Question wording and all four options checked against official GSET September 2013 Paper-II PDF, printed page 21 (PDF page 21). Answer D matches the official corrected key. Answer checked against the repository's official GSET final answer-key transcription; question wording/options remain unverified against the original question paper.
tip_en: For joint upper-tail probabilities, use complement and inclusion-exclusion.
tip_gu: Joint upper-tail probability માટે complement અને inclusion-exclusion વાપરો.
source: Official GSET Mathematical Sciences Paper-II, September 2013

(B) \(\mathbb{Q}\setminus\{q\in\mathbb{Q}\mid 0<q<1\}\) is countable. (C) The set of all sequences of zeros and ones is countable. (D) There exist countably many pairwise disjoint uncountable subsets of \(\mathbb{R}\).
options_en: There are countably many pairwise disjoint countable subsets of \(\mathbb{R}\)
The set of all sequences of zeros and ones is countable
There exist countably many pairwise disjoint uncountable subsets of \(\mathbb{R}\)
options_gu: There are countably many pairwise disjoint countable subsets of \(\mathbb{R}\)
The set of all sequences of zeros and ones is countable
There exist countably many pairwise disjoint uncountable subsets of \(\mathbb{R}\)
explanation_en: The set of all infinite binary sequences is uncountable. If the sequences were listed as s₁, s₂, …, construct a new sequence whose n-th digit differs from the n-th digit of sₙ. This diagonal sequence is missing from the list. Therefore statement (C) is false.
explanation_gu: શૂન્ય અને એકથી બનેલી બધી અનંત sequencesનો સમૂહ uncountable છે. જો તેમને (s_1,s_2,ldots) તરીકે યાદીબદ્ધ કરીએ, તો નવી sequence એવી બનાવી શકાય કે તેની nમી digit, (s_n)ની nમી digitથી અલગ હોય. આ નવી sequence યાદીમાં નથી આવતી (Cantor diagonal argument). તેથી (C) ખોટું છે.
review_note: Answer checked against the repository's official GSET final answer-key transcription; question wording/options remain unverified against the original question paper.
tip_en: Remember: the set of finite binary strings is countable, but the set of all infinite binary sequences is uncountable.
tip_gu: યાદ રાખો: finite binary stringsનો સમૂહ countable છે, પરંતુ તમામ infinite binary sequencesનો સમૂહ uncountable છે.
source: GSET official September 2016 Mathematical Sciences Paper-II and official final/corrected answer key

question_en: Which of the following is an eigenvector for the matrix \(A=\begin{bmatrix}1&0&1\\0&2&0\\0&0&3\end{bmatrix}\)?
question_gu: Which of the following is an eigenvector for the matrix \(A=\begin{bmatrix}1&0&1\\0&2&0\\0&0&3\end{bmatrix}\)?
explanation_en: An eigenvector v must satisfy Av = λv for some scalar λ. For option (B), v = [1, 0, 0]ᵀ and Av = [1, 0, 0]ᵀ = 1v. Hence it is an eigenvector with eigenvalue λ = 1. The other listed vectors do not satisfy Av = λv for this matrix.
explanation_gu: Eigenvector (v) માટે (Av=\lambda v) હોવું જોઈએ. વિકલ્પ (B) માટે (v=(1,0,0)^T) છે અને (Av=(1,0,0)^T=1v). તેથી તે eigenvalue (lambda=1) માટે eigenvector છે.
review_note: Answer checked against the repository's official GSET final answer-key transcription; question wording/options remain unverified against the original question paper.
tip_en: Check a proposed eigenvector by multiplying the matrix by the vector and testing whether the result is a scalar multiple of the original vector.

question_en: If \(f(z)=\dfrac{(2-e^z-e^{-z})^k}{z^7}\) has a simple pole at the origin, then the value of \(k\) is:
question_gu: If \(f(z)=\dfrac{(2-e^z-e^{-z})^k}{z^7}\) has a simple pole at the origin, then the value of \(k\) is:
explanation_en: Using the expansions eᶻ = 1 + z + z²/2 + … and e⁻ᶻ = 1 − z + z²/2 + …, we get 2 − eᶻ − e⁻ᶻ = −z² + higher-order terms, so the numerator has a zero of order 2k. Dividing by z⁷ gives pole order 7 − 2k. A simple pole has order 1, so 7 − 2k = 1 and k = 3.
explanation_gu: (e^z=1+z+\frac{z^2}{2}+cdots) અને (e^{-z}=1-z+\frac{z^2}{2}+cdots) વાપરીએ તો (2-e^z-e^{-z}=-z^2+cdots). એટલે numeratorમાં (2k) ક્રમનો zero છે. (z^7)થી ભાગતાં poleનો ક્રમ (7-2k) થાય છે. Simple pole માટે (7-2k=1), તેથી (k=3).
review_note: Answer checked against the repository's official GSET final answer-key transcription; question wording/options remain unverified against the original question paper.
tip_en: For a pole-order question, find the order of the zero in the numerator first, then subtract it from the denominator's zero order.
tip_gu: Poleનો ક્રમ શોધવા પહેલાં numeratorમાં zeroનો ક્રમ શોધો અને denominatorના zeroના ક્રમમાંથી ઘટાડો.
source: GSET official September 2016 Mathematical Sciences Paper-II and official final/corrected answer key

question_en: If \(C[0,1]\) is the space of continuous functions with metric \(d(f,g)=\sup_{x\in[0,1]}|f(x)-g(x)|\), then \(d(x,x^2)\) is equal to:
question_gu: If \(C[0,1]\) is the space of continuous functions with metric \(d(f,g)=\sup_{x\in[0,1]}|f(x)-g(x)|\), then \(d(x,x^2)\) is equal to:
explanation_en: By the given metric, d(x, x²) = sup₀≤x≤₁ |x − x²|. On [0, 1], x − x² = x(1 − x) ≥ 0. The quadratic reaches its maximum at x = 1/2 (or by differentiating, 1 − 2x = 0). The maximum is 1/2 − 1/4 = 1/4. Therefore option (A) is correct.
explanation_gu: આ metric પ્રમાણે (d(x,x^2)=\sup_{x\in[0,1]}|x-x^2|). ([0,1]) પર (x-x^2=x(1-x)\ge0). તેનું મહત્તમ (x=\frac12) પર મળે છે, કારણ કે derivative (1-2x=0) થાય છે. તેથી મહત્તમ મૂલ્ય (\frac12-\frac14=\frac14) છે. સાચો જવાબ (A).
review_note: Answer checked against the repository's official GSET final answer-key transcription; question wording/options remain unverified against the original question paper.
tip_en: For a supremum on a closed interval, inspect critical points and endpoints.
tip_gu: Closed interval પર supremum શોધતી વખતે critical points અને endpoints બંને તપાસો.
source: GSET official September 2016 Mathematical Sciences Paper-II and official final/corrected answer key

question_en: Consider a random variable \(X\) with \(P(X=1)=\frac18=P(X=-1)\) and \(P(X=0)=\frac38=P(X=2)\). What is the value of \(E\!\left[\frac{X}{X+4}\right]\)?
question_gu: Consider a random variable \(X\) with \(P(X=1)=\frac18=P(X=-1)\) and \(P(X=0)=\frac38=P(X=2)\). What is the value of \(E\!\left[\frac{X}{X+4}\right]\)?
explanation_gu: (E[g(X)]=\sum g(x)P(X=x)) વાપરીએ, જ્યાં (g(x)=\frac{x}{x+4}). તેથી (E[\frac{X}{X+4}]=\frac18\frac15+\frac18(-\frac13)+\frac38(0)+\frac38(\frac13)). એટલે (\frac1{40}-\frac1{24}+\frac18=\frac{3-5+15}{120}=\frac{13}{120}). સાચો જવાબ (C).
review_note: Answer checked against the repository's official GSET final answer-key transcription; question wording/options remain unverified against the original question paper.
tip_en: For a discrete random variable, multiply each function value by its probability and add all terms.
tip_gu: Discrete random variable માટે દરેક function valueને તેની probabilityથી ગુણો અને બધા termsનો સરવાળો કરો.
source: GSET official September 2016 Mathematical Sciences Paper-II and official final/corrected answer key

question_en: To compare the lifetimes of bulbs produced by two companies, A and B, one bulb of each company was selected at random and their lifetimes were observed. Assume that the bulbs have exponentially distributed lifetimes with mean 1000 days for company A and 800 days for company B. What is the probability that the bulb from company B fails first?
question_gu: To compare the lifetimes of bulbs produced by two companies, A and B, one bulb of each company was selected at random and their lifetimes were observed. Assume that the bulbs have exponentially distributed lifetimes with mean 1000 days for company A and 800 days for company B. What is the probability that the bulb from company B fails first?
explanation_en: For an exponential lifetime, the failure rate is the reciprocal of the mean: λA = 1/1000 and λB = 1/800. For independent exponential lifetimes, P(B fails first) = λB/(λA + λB) = (1/800)/(1/1000 + 1/800) = 5/9. Option (B).
explanation_gu: Exponential lifetime માટે failure rate meanનો reciprocal છે: (\lambda_A=\frac1{1000}), (\lambda_B=\frac1{800}). Independent exponential lifetimesમાં B પહેલાં fail થવાની probability (\frac{\lambda_B}{\lambda_A+\lambda_B}=\frac{1/800}{1/1000+1/800}=\frac59) થાય છે. સાચો જવાબ (B).
review_note: Answer checked against the repository's official GSET final answer-key transcription; question wording/options remain unverified against the original question paper.
tip_en: For independent exponential lifetimes, the probability that one fails first equals its rate divided by the sum of the rates.
tip_gu: Independent exponential lifetimesમાં કોઈ એક પહેલાં fail થવાની probability તેની rateને બંને ratesના સરવાળાથી ભાગવાથી મળે છે.
source: GSET official September 2016 Mathematical Sciences Paper-II and official final/corrected answer key
